heard: A dormant supermassive black hole fired a particle jet directly at Earth. Most cosmic blasts fade within seconds, but NASA's Swift satellite detected a source that flared repeatedly with intense x-rays for days. In the northern constellation Draco, an approaching star was gravitationally ripped completely to shreds. The shredder was a dormant supermassive black hole lurking inside the core of a distant galaxy. As stellar debris fell into an accretion disk, it launched a particle jet traveling near the speed of light. That relativistic jet crossed 3.8 billion light years with its narrow beam aimed directly toward Earth. This head-on alignment significantly amplified its brightness, generating extraordinarily luminous and long-lived X-ray emissions. Astronomers were staring straight down the barrel of a monstrous cosmic shredder.
